question: Should Slack deliberately suppress typed progress payloads when no usable thread reaction target exists or reaction conversion fails?
rationale: The code can implement either policy, but choosing silent suppression over the currently visible message behavior is a compatibility and product decision that tests cannot resolve.

options.title: Approve fail-closed suppression
options.body: Accept silent suppression for typed progress after current-head agent-turn proof demonstrates the controls and delivery-state invariants.

options.title: Preserve message fallback
options.body: Post typed progress normally whenever reaction conversion is unavailable, preserving current visibility at the cost of progress noise.

options.title: Pause for portable presentation
options.body: Defer this branch and design a broader typed channel presentation action before changing Slack delivery semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed suppression
recommendation.body: Accept silent suppression for typed progress after current-head agent-turn proof demonstrates the controls and delivery-state invariants.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the broadest ownership of Slack reply dispatch, threading, fallback, and Plugin SDK boundary decisions affected by this policy.
